triples.relationship: explicit command to leave Babylon
triples.rationale: Zechariah commands those dwelling in daughter Babylon to escape safely to Zion. Isaiah likewise commands leaving Babylon and fleeing the Chaldeans while announcing the Lord's rescue of Jacob. The named place and commanded departure connect the passages.
triples.source_text: Escape safely to Zion, you who dwell in daughter Babylon!

target_units.text: Leave Babylon, fleeing from the Chaldeans. Announce a voice of rejoicing, and let this be heard; proclaim it to the earth’s extremity. Say, “The Lord rescued His slave Jacob.”

triples.relationship: God's people compared with the vulnerable pupil of an eye
triples.rationale: Zechariah says touching the plundered people is like touching an eye's pupil. Deuteronomy describes the Lord guarding His people Jacob as an eye's pupil. Both use that particular bodily image to express the people's protected importance.
triples.source_text: For thus says the Lord Almighty: “After glory He has sent me against the nations that plundered you, for whoever touches you is like one touching the pupil of his eye.

target_units.text: And His people Jacob became the portion of the Lord; Israel, the measured lot of His inheritance.
He sustained him in a wilderness land, in the thirst of burning heat, in a waterless place; He compassed him about, and instructed him, and kept him as the pupil of an eye.

triples.relationship: eye-pupil imagery in a setting of protection from enemies
triples.rationale: Zechariah warns the nations that touching the people is like touching an eye's pupil. The psalm asks God to guard the speaker as an eye's pupil amid surrounding enemies. Both connect the vulnerable eye image with protection from hostility.
triples.source_text: For thus says the Lord Almighty: “After glory He has sent me against the nations that plundered you, for whoever touches you is like one touching the pupil of his eye.

target_units.text: Make Thy mercies wonderful, Thou who savest those hoping in Thee from those who oppose Thy right hand.
Guard me as the pupil of an eye; in the shelter of Thy wings Thou wilt shelter me,
from the ungodly who made me miserable. My enemies surrounded my soul.

triples.relationship: reversal of the relation between captors and servants
triples.rationale: Zechariah announces that the plundering nations will become spoils for those serving them. Isaiah likewise says former captors will become captives and former rulers will be ruled, followed by rest from harsh slavery. Both expressly reverse domination.
triples.source_text: Look, I am bringing My hand against them, and they will become spoils for those serving them; you will know that the Lord Almighty has sent me.”

target_units.text: and nations will take them and bring them into their place; they will inherit and multiply upon God’s land as male and female slaves. Those who took them captive will be captives, and those who ruled them will be ruled.
On that day God will give you rest from pain, your wrath and the harsh slavery in which you served them,

triples.relationship: daughter Zion called to rejoice because the Lord is within her
triples.rationale: Zechariah calls daughter Zion to delight and rejoice because the Lord will come and dwell within her. Zephaniah similarly calls Zion and Jerusalem to rejoice and names the saving Lord within her. The address, joy and divine presence closely correspond.
triples.source_text: “Delight and rejoice, daughter Zion, for look, I am coming and will dwell within you,” says the Lord.

target_units.text: Rejoice greatly, daughter Zion! Proclaim, daughter Jerusalem! Be glad and delight with all your heart, daughter Jerusalem!
The Lord removed your wrongdoings and has redeemed you from your enemies’ hand. The Lord, King of Israel, is within you; you will see evils no more.
At that time the Lord will say to Jerusalem, “Take courage, Zion; do not let your hands hang loose.
The Lord your God is within you; mighty, He shall save you. He shall bring gladness upon you, and renew you in His love; and He shall rejoice over you with delight, as on a day of feasting.”

triples.relationship: nations and foreigners welcomed into the Lord's restored community
triples.rationale: Zechariah promises that many nations will take refuge with the Lord and become His people. Isaiah welcomes foreigners attached to the Lord into His holy mountain and house of prayer for all nations. Both place people from other nations within the Lord's gathered community.
triples.source_text: Many nations will take refuge with the Lord on that day and become His people. They will dwell within you, and you will recognize that the Lord Almighty has sent me to you.

target_units.text: And the foreigners attached to the Lord, to serve Him and love the Lord’s name, to become His male and female slaves, and all those keeping My Sabbaths from profanation and holding fast to My covenant—

I will bring them into My holy mountain and make them rejoice in My house of prayer. Their whole burnt offerings and sacrifices will be acceptable on My altar, for My house will be called a house of prayer for all nations,”
said the Lord who gathers Israel’s scattered people, “for I will gather a gathering to him.”

triples.relationship: the Lord's people described as His portion and inheritance
triples.rationale: Zechariah calls Judah the Lord's portion on the holy land. Deuteronomy likewise calls Jacob His portion and Israel the measured lot of His inheritance. The comparison concerns that stated belonging, while preserving each passage's named people.
triples.source_text: The Lord will inherit Judah as His portion on the holy land and again choose Jerusalem.

target_units.text: And His people Jacob became the portion of the Lord; Israel, the measured lot of His inheritance.

triples.relationship: universal reverence before the Lord in His holy dwelling
triples.rationale: Zechariah calls all flesh to reverence because the Lord has risen from His holy clouds. Habakkuk calls all the earth to revere Him in His holy sanctuary. Both combine a universal summons to reverence with His holy dwelling, described differently.
triples.source_text: Let all flesh be reverent before the Lord, for He has risen from His holy clouds.

target_units.text: But the Lord is in His holy sanctuary; let all the earth revere Him.”

triples.relationship: a slanderer positioned at the accused person's right hand
triples.rationale: Joshua stands before the Lord's angel with the slanderer at his right hand to oppose him. The psalm likewise pictures a slanderer standing at someone's right hand in a context of judgment. The position and accusatory role connect the scenes.
triples.source_text: He showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the Lord, with the slanderer standing at his right hand to oppose him.

target_units.text: Appoint a sinner over him, and let a slanderer stand at his right hand.
When he is judged, may he come out condemned, and let his prayer become sin.

triples.relationship: an adversary challenges a servant before God
triples.rationale: Zechariah's vision places the slanderer beside Joshua to oppose him before the Lord's angel. Job likewise presents the devil among God's angels challenging the motives of God's servant Job. Both feature an adversary bringing a challenge concerning a named servant, without equating the servants or proceedings.
triples.source_text: He showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the Lord, with the slanderer standing at his right hand to oppose him.

target_units.text: When that day came, behold, the angels of God came to stand before the Lord, and the devil came with them.
The Lord said to the devil, “Where have you come from?” The devil answered the Lord, “I have come after going around the earth and walking through the world beneath heaven.”
The Lord said to him, “Have you paid attention in your mind to My servant Job? For among those on earth there is no man like him—blameless, true, God-fearing, keeping away from every evil deed.”
The devil answered before the Lord, “Does Job worship God for nothing?

Hast Thou not fenced in what is outside him and what is inside his house, and everything around all that belongs to him? Thou hast blessed the works of his hands and made his livestock numerous in the land.
But stretch out Thy hand and touch everything he has; surely he will curse Thee to Thy face.”

triples.relationship: shared appeal for the Lord to rebuke an adversary
triples.rationale: Zechariah addresses the slanderer with the words 'May the Lord rebuke you.' Jude reports Michael using the same appeal while disputing with the devil concerning Moses' body. The verbal correspondence is explicit, while the occasions differ.
triples.source_text: The Lord said to the slanderer, “May the Lord rebuke you, slanderer! May the Lord, who chose Jerusalem, rebuke you! Look, is this not like a brand pulled from fire?”

target_units.text: But Michael the archangel, when he was contending with the devil and disputing about the body of Moses, did not dare to bring a slanderous judgment against him, but said, “May the Lord rebuke you.”

triples.relationship: shared image of a brand pulled from fire
triples.rationale: The question concerning Joshua likens him to a brand pulled from fire. Amos likewise describes the people as a firebrand snatched from fire after an overthrow. Both use the particular rescue image, with different persons and settings.
triples.source_text: The Lord said to the slanderer, “May the Lord rebuke you, slanderer! May the Lord, who chose Jerusalem, rebuke you! Look, is this not like a brand pulled from fire?”

target_units.text: “I overthrew you as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and you became like a firebrand snatched from fire. Yet not even so did you turn to Me,” says the Lord.

triples.relationship: unclean clothing associated with lawlessness
triples.rationale: Joshua's filthy garments are interpreted in the next unit through the removal of his lawless deeds. Isaiah likewise links the people's uncleanness and rag-like righteousness with their lawless deeds. Both use soiled clothing imagery in describing a sinful condition, without identifying their garments as the same object.
triples.source_text: Joshua was clothed in filthy garments and standing before the angel.

target_units.text: We all became like unclean people; all our righteousness is like a menstruating woman’s rag. We fell away like leaves because of our lawless deeds; thus wind will carry us off.

triples.relationship: new clothing expressing divine restoration
triples.rationale: Joshua's filthy garments are removed as his lawless deeds are taken away, and he is clothed in a full-length robe. Isaiah's speaker likewise rejoices in being clothed by the Lord with salvation and joy. Both associate new clothing with divine restoration, while naming the garments differently.
triples.source_text: He answered and said to those standing before him, “Remove the filthy garments from him.” He said to him, “Look, I have taken away your lawless deeds; clothe him in a robe reaching to the feet,

target_units.text: and they will rejoice greatly in the Lord.” Let my soul exult in the Lord, for He clothed me in a garment of salvation and a tunic of joy. Like a bridegroom He placed a turban on me, and like a bride He adorned me with ornaments.

triples.relationship: the high priest clothed with a robe and turban
triples.rationale: Joshua receives clean headwear and garments in his role as high priest. Exodus prescribes holy priestly garments for Aaron, including a full-length robe and turban. The shared priestly dress connects the scenes; Zechariah adds cleansing within the vision.
triples.source_text: and put a clean turban on his head.” They clothed him in garments and put a clean turban on his head, while the angel of the Lord stood by.

target_units.text: “And bring to yourself Aaron your brother and his sons from among the sons of Israel, to serve Me as priests: Aaron, and Nadab, and Abihu, and Eleazar, and Ithamar, the sons of Aaron.
You shall make a holy robe for Aaron your brother, for honour and glory.
Speak to everyone skilled in understanding whom I have filled with a spirit of perception. They shall make Aaron’s holy robe for the sanctuary, in which he shall serve Me as priest.

These are the robes they shall make: a breastpiece, a shoulder-piece, a full-length robe, a tasselled tunic, a turban, and a sash. They shall make holy robes for Aaron and his sons to serve Me as priests.

triples.relationship: priestly responsibility for keeping the sanctuary's charge
triples.rationale: Joshua is charged to keep the Lord's commands and guard His court as he governs His house. Numbers likewise assigns priestly and Levitical service to keeping the charges and furnishings of the Tent. Both connect religious office with responsibility for the sanctuary.
triples.source_text: “Thus says the Lord Almighty: If you walk in My ways and keep My commands, you will govern My house. If you also guard My court, I will give you those who move about among these standing here.

target_units.text: Take the tribe of Levi, and you shall set them before Aaron the priest, and they shall minister unto him;
And they shall keep his charges and the charges of the sons of Israel before the Tent of Testimony, performing the work of the Tent.
And they shall keep all the furnishings of the Tent of Testimony and the charges of the sons of Israel, according to all the work of the Tent.
And you shall give the Levites unto Aaron and unto his sons, the priests. These are given unto Me as a gift from the sons of Israel.

And you shall appoint Aaron and his sons over the Tent of Testimony, and they shall keep their priesthood, and all that concerns the altar and is within the veil. And the outsider who touches shall die.

triples.relationship: same-book recurrence of the promised figure named Rising
triples.rationale: The Lord promises to bring His servant Rising before Joshua and his companions. Chapter 6 again announces a man named Rising and says he will build the Lord's house. The repeated name connects the two announcements.
triples.source_text: Listen now, Joshua the high priest, you and your neighbors sitting before you, for they are men who watch for portents. Look, I am bringing My servant, Rising.

target_units.text: and say to him: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Look, a man whose name is Rising! From beneath him he will rise, and he will build the Lord’s house.

triples.relationship: a future rising announced by the Lord
triples.rationale: Zechariah announces the coming servant named Rising. Jeremiah likewise announces that the Lord will raise a righteous rising for David who will reign and practice judgment. Both use the rising expression for an anticipated figure, while their respective stated descriptions are preserved.
triples.source_text: Listen now, Joshua the high priest, you and your neighbors sitting before you, for they are men who watch for portents. Look, I am bringing My servant, Rising.

target_units.text: Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will raise up a righteous rising for David. A king will reign and understand, doing judgment and righteousness upon the earth.

triples.relationship: same-book visionary motif of seven eyes
triples.rationale: Zechariah 3 presents a stone with seven eyes. Chapter 4 identifies seven as the Lord's eyes looking over all the earth. The shared seven-eye motif connects the visions, without turning chapter 3's pit and feeling out injustice into wording it does not contain.
triples.source_text: For the stone I set before Joshua—on the one stone are seven eyes. Look, I am digging a pit, says the Lord Almighty, and I will feel out all the injustice of that land in one day.

target_units.text: For who treated the small days with contempt? They will rejoice and see the tin stone in Zerubbabel’s hand. These seven are the Lord’s eyes, looking over all the earth.”

triples.relationship: peaceful life beneath vine and fig tree
triples.rationale: Zechariah promises neighbors inviting one another beneath a vine and fig tree. Micah likewise describes each person resting beneath his vine and fig tree without fear. Both use those paired plants to picture restored communal peace.
triples.source_text: On that day, says the Lord Almighty, each of you will invite his neighbor beneath a vine and beneath a fig tree.”

target_units.text: Each will rest beneath his vine and each beneath his fig tree, and there will be no one causing fear, because the mouth of the Lord Almighty has spoken these things.

triples.relationship: a visionary restored from sleep before receiving an explanation
triples.rationale: Zechariah describes the angel rousing him as someone awakened from sleep before the next vision. Daniel likewise falls asleep while the interpreter speaks and is touched and raised before further explanation. The comparison concerns the visionary's restoration to attention.
triples.source_text: The angel speaking within me returned and roused me as when someone is awakened from sleep,

target_units.text: He came and stood beside where I stood. As he came, I was disturbed and fell upon my face. He said to me, “Understand, son of man, for this vision is still for an appointed hour.”
As he spoke with me, I fell asleep face down on the ground. He touched me and raised me on the spot,
and said to me, “Behold! I am reporting what will happen at the end of the wrath to the sons of your people; it will still remain until the hours of the appointed time of completion.

triples.relationship: a golden lampstand carrying seven lamps
triples.rationale: Zechariah sees an entirely golden lampstand with seven lamps. Exodus prescribes a lampstand of pure gold and specifically commands seven lamps upon it. The common material and seven lamps connect the vision with sanctuary furnishings, without equating every added channel or bowl.
triples.source_text: and said to me, “What do you see?” I said, “I see a lampstand entirely of gold, with its lamp-bowl above it, seven lamps upon it, and seven pouring channels for the lamps above it.

target_units.text: You shall make a lampstand of pure gold, of worked metal. Its stem, branches, bowls, knobs, and lilies shall be made from it.
Six branches shall extend from its sides, three from one side of the lampstand and three from the other.
There shall be three bowls shaped like little nuts, with a knob and lily on one branch. So it shall be for the six branches extending from the lampstand.
On the lampstand there shall be four bowls shaped like little nuts; on one branch shall be its knobs and lilies.
There shall be a knob under the two branches extending from it, and a knob under the four branches extending from it; so it shall be for the six branches extending from the lampstand.
Its knobs and branches shall be made from it, the whole worked from one piece of pure gold.
You shall make its seven lamps and set them on it, and they shall shine from one face.

triples.relationship: same-chapter olive trees revisited for interpretation
triples.rationale: The vision first places two olive trees to the lampstand's right and left. Zechariah later asks about those two trees, and the angel answers with two sons of richness standing beside the Lord. The later dialogue explicitly returns to the initially described pair.
triples.source_text: Two olive trees stand over it, one to the right of the lamp-bowl and one to the left.”

target_units.text: I answered him, “What are these two olive trees to the lampstand’s right and left?”
I asked a second time, “What are the two olive branches in the hands of the two golden nozzles that pour upon and draw up the golden pouring channels?”
He said to me, “Do you not know what these are?” I said, “No, lord.”
He said, “These two sons of richness stand beside the Lord of all the earth.”

triples.relationship: Zerubbabel encouraged through the presence of God's Spirit
triples.rationale: The word to Zerubbabel locates the decisive agency in the Lord's Spirit rather than great power or strength. Haggai likewise tells Zerubbabel and the builders to work courageously because the Lord is with them and His Spirit stands in their midst. Both address the rebuilding setting with assurance of the Spirit's presence.
triples.source_text: He answered me, “This is the Lord’s word to Zerubbabel: Not by great power or by strength, but by My Spirit, says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: But now be strong, Zerubbabel, says the Lord; be strong, Joshua, son of Jehozadak, the high priest; let all the people of the land be strong, says the Lord, and work, for I am with you, says the Lord Almighty,
and My Spirit stands in your midst. Take courage.

triples.relationship: the foundation of the rebuilt Lord's house
triples.rationale: Zechariah recalls Zerubbabel's hands laying the house's foundation and promises its completion. Ezra's account places Zorobabel among those beginning the work and then describes the foundation being laid with public thanksgiving. The shared rebuilding and foundation connect the accounts while their name forms are preserved.
triples.source_text: “Zerubbabel’s hands laid this house’s foundation, and his hands will complete it. You will recognize that the Lord Almighty has sent me to you.

target_units.text: In the second year after their arrival at the house of God in Jerusalem, in the second month, Zorobabel son of Salathiel, Iesous son of Iosedek, the rest of their brothers the priests and Levites, and all who had come from captivity to Jerusalem began. They set the Levites from twenty years old and upward over those doing the work in the Lord’s house.
Iesous and his sons and his brothers, Kadmiel and his sons, sons of Judah, stood over those doing the work in the house of God; also the sons of Enadad, their sons and their brothers the Levites.

They laid the foundation for building the Lord’s house, and the priests stood in their vestments with trumpets, and the Levites, sons of Asaph, with cymbals, to praise the Lord according to the directions of David king of Israel.

They answered in praise and thanksgiving to the Lord: “For it is good, for His mercy toward Israel endures for ever.” All the people sounded a great cry of praise to the Lord at the founding of the Lord’s house.
